sources_quoted.quote: Enemy champions within 700 units of you become cursed, causing them to receive 12% increased magic damage from all sources. — confirmed: magic damage ONLY (not all damage types); applies to damage from allies as well; conditional on the 700-unit range from the item holder.

independent_computation.step_1_magnitude: Unmake's amplifier is 12% => multiplier = 1 + 12/100 = 1.12. Confirmed three ways in the cache (passives[0].branches[0] wiki text, riotDescription, atoms values [700.0, 12.0] with units [flat, percent]) and once live on the wiki. So the NUMBER 1.12 in the old leaf is not itself a mis-parse.
independent_computation.step_2_preconditions: The 1.12 is not unconditional. The quoted text makes it conditional on three predicates, all of which must hold for the amplifier to be authored onto a damage event: (a) the damaged unit is an enemy CHAMPION; (b) that champion is within 700 units (center-to-edge) of the Abyssal Mask HOLDER — in this scenario an ally on the roster, not the attacker, so the geometry is holder-relative, not attacker-relative; (c) the damage instance being amplified is MAGIC damage. Predicate (c) is the sharp one: 'increased magic damage' / 'take 12% more magic damage' restricts the amp by damage type. Physical and true damage receive no amplification from Unmake. (Contrast Imperial Mandate's Command, whose 7% is explicitly 'damage they take from all sources' — type-agnostic — which is precisely why a scenario named mandate_abyssal_curse_roster pairs the two: one type-agnostic amp and one magic-only amp on the same roster.)
independent_computation.step_3_correct_leaf_value: correct(support_damage_multiplier @ event) = 1.12 if the event is magic damage dealt to a cursed enemy champion whose 700-unit proximity to the ally holder is established; otherwise the leaf must be ABSENT. There is no sourced value between those two — in particular nothing in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md supports a partial or type-blind application of Unmake.
independent_computation.step_4_which_branch_applies_to_events[7]: The old leaf carried source 'Abyssal Mask — Unmake' alone, with no Imperial Mandate contribution, i.e. the engine authored the magic-only amp as a standalone per-event multiplier. Absence is the correct state on this event under either sourced failure of a precondition: (i) events[7] is not a magic-damage instance — the wiki text then forbids the amp outright, and a magic-only amplifier applied to a physical/true event is exactly the type-blind-amplification defect the quoted text rules out; or (ii) the 700-unit predicate for an ALLY-held aura is not established by the fight model, which carries no positioning — in which case the amp must be withheld rather than assumed, matching the repo's own fail-closed doctrine for effects whose sourcing conditions are missing. Conversely, the old value can only be defended by asserting BOTH that events[7] is magic damage AND that the ally holder's 700-unit proximity is established; neither assertion is derivable from any cached source. An amplifier is authored on positive evidence, not on the absence of a disproof, so 1.12 was the unsupported state and <absent> is the supported one.
independent_computation.step_5_cross_check_on_composition: A further check against the old value: if the ally's Imperial Mandate Vulnerable mark were live on the same event, the correct combined support amplifier would be 1.07 x 1.12 = 1.1984 (or 1.19 additively), not 1.12 with a single Abyssal source. So 1.12-with-Abyssal-source-only is defensible only in the sub-case where Mandate's immobilize precondition is unmet. That narrows, rather than supports, the old value; it does not rescue it.

confidence_and_limits: The magnitude (1.12) and the qualifying conditions (enemy champion, 700 units from the holder, MAGIC damage only) are established at high confidence from four independent cached artifacts plus a live wiki fetch. What the permitted evidence tree cannot show is the damage type of combat/events[7] itself: the scenario 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' is defined in scripts/ (golden snapshot), which this runbook forbids reading, and it is absent from data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json (22 scenarios, none matching). The verdict therefore rests on the asymmetry in step 4 — the amp requires positive evidence of a magic-damage instance under an in-range curse, and no cached source establishes that for this event — rather than on a direct reading of the event's type. If an inspection of the scenario definition shows events[7] to be a magic-damage instance against a cursed champion with the holder's range modeled, this verdict should be revisited to old_value_correct.
